DRI / Project owner Mention DRI of the project using @... Team List team members using @... Pitch Context & Idea Goal. Raise ARPU on the iOS paywalls for the top propensity decile by opening the product tier they can afford, instead of the cheaper tier they currently default into. Idea. Restore the Pro / Premium tabbed paywall and open the Premium tab by default for the top propensity decile, on both the tour paywall and the feature paywalls. Every other segment opens on the Pro tab by default. Observed behaviour. The cheap path is real, but it is not on the tour paywall. Re-measured 2026-08-10 on the matured cohort (method under Data verification below): over 15 days the segment took 1,635 UG Plus subscriptions (1,235 paid, $22.09 each) against 3,264 bundle subscriptions (1,872 paid, $50.59 each) — yet on funnel_source = 'Tour Install' 2,646 of 2,647 purchases were the bundle. The tour paywall shows this segment nothing else: 9,939 Banner Tour View events over 7 days carry only pro_edu_sing SKUs. The cheapest SKU in the mix, ugt.plus.instant.1year3 ($22.93, 152 paid subs / 15 days), occurs only on Tour Post Decline Instant Offer ; the rest of the cheap path sits on feature paywalls and ad interstitials. The off-tour value gap is confirmed: top-segment ARPPU is $23.09 on feature paywalls against $47.70 on the tour paywall (exp 7568). Why the top decile. Exp 7568 established that this segment is not price-constrained. When the tour paywall switched to instant-default, top-decile ARPU rose 30% ($3.69 → $4.80, p<0.001) through more buyers — buyer rate +24.7% (10.1% → 12.6%, p<0.001) at an almost flat revenue per buyer ($36.62 → $38.20, +4.3%) — the segment absorbed a higher payment bar without paying more per head. The constraint tested here is not price tolerance but which product is presented first. Why now. The tab layer has never been read. Iteration 3 of the parent project collected one day of data and was ruled unusable, so the layout was shelved without evidence. Meanwhile the propensity score from exp 7568 is in production and persists on the device, which makes a per-segment default possible on surfaces beyond the tour for the first time. Scope. iOS only. Audience: segment = top and score >= -1 — verified at 1,373 users/day on the tour (measured 1,338/day in July 2026 and 1,366/day over 2026-07-01..08-09) plus the same users on feature paywalls. Note that this is 14.2% of daily iOS tour paywall viewers, not a decile ( segment = top alone is 35.0%); "top decile" in this document means the score-capped top segment. The score is the existing frozen scorecard; no model work is in scope. Note on the tab precedent. Iteration 3 split its tabs by duration (monthly / yearly), not by product tier. Pro and Premium are two different products sold on two different surfaces, so the iteration 3 mockups are reusable as a UI pattern only, not as a validated layout. Questions & Answers Question Status What is sold in the Premium tab on a feature paywall, and at what price? Blocking for the feature surface. The iteration 2–3 price list carries no bundle SKU on feature paywalls at any price. Either a price is set, or the feature surface leaves version 1. Does the treatment arm change one thing or two? Open. No tabs exist in production today, so the treatment restores the tab layer and sets the default tab. A two-arm test measures the package and cannot attribute the effect to the default. A three-arm test (no tabs / tabs with Pro default / tabs with Premium default) separates them, at ~13.5 days of enrollment instead of 6.3 for the same MDE once α is split across comparisons. Do the Pro and Premium tabs keep the monthly/yearly split inside them? Open. Duration was the tab axis in iteration 3; if it is retained, the tabs nest and the mockup set doubles. Is the non-top policy measured? Open. Pro-by-default reaches roughly 86% of iOS tour traffic (the targeted segment is 14.2%, measured 2026-08-10), but the stated baseline — now $6.89 — covers only the targeted segment. As written, the majority policy ships without a read. Is "no drop in overall subscription conversion" a hypothesis condition or a guardrail? Open. In exp 7568 subscription conversion fell by design (top Click→Sub 59.8% → 51.6%, tour subs −20%) and was accepted, because each instant subscriber paid immediately. If the same trade appears here, the current wording would fail the experiment on its own terms. Recommended: move it to a guardrail with a defined threshold. When does the feature surface start? Blocking outside the tour. UMN-12572 (score = 0 fallback qualification) must land first, otherwise the off-tour "top" is 89% legacy base. Are the guardrail thresholds defined? Gap. Refund 14d, cancel 14d, retention 7/14d, tour skip and store rating are named, but no failure threshold is set for any of them. Confidence research Medium-high on the segment, low on the mechanism. Evidence Relevance to this hypothesis Limitation Top-decile ARPU +30% with flat ARPPU under instant-default (exp 7568) Shows the segment converts under a harder payment bar without price resistance, which is the premise for offering the more expensive product first Measures payment timing, not product tier. It does not establish that the same users would accept a 2.5x more expensive bundle Top ARPPU $23.09 off-tour against $47.70 on-tour (exp 7568) Quantifies where the value is lost The bundle is not in the feature price list at all, so the gap is partly a catalogue gap, not only a default-tab gap. This weakens "the default pushes them down" as the sole explanation 1,235 paid UG Plus subscriptions / 15 days into the cheap path = 82/day (measured 2026-08-10) Direct observation of the leak the change targets, now sized across all surfaces Observational — and none of it is on the tour paywall : 0 of the 1,235 came from Tour Install . 152 are ugt.plus.instant.1year3 on the post-decline instant offer, which this document lists as out of scope; the remainder are feature paywalls and ad interstitials. The cohort's cheapest annual SKU is ugt.plus.instant.1year3 Iteration 3 tabs unusable after 1 day (#7115) The reason the layer is worth retesting rather than assumed dead Iteration 3 tabs split by duration, not product tier — no UG precedent exists for a Pro/Premium tab split Scorecard validated forward, ROC-AUC 0.67, top/bottom ARPI 4.7x The targeting substrate is sound and already shipped Cutpoints frozen on May 2026 data; score >= -1 is an absolute threshold, so segment composition moves if the scorecard is reweighted Counter-evidence to hold in view. Exp 7568 found that the middle third underdelivered against its model-derived forecast (+41% expected, +6.8% realised, not significant), while the top third beat it. Model-derived per-segment forecasts on this population have already proved optimistic once. Conclusion: the segment premise is supported. The mechanism premise is not, and measurement has now narrowed it: the tour paywall carries no cheap-path volume to shift, so a prospective test is worth running only on the surfaces that do — or on the tour explicitly as a defensive read. Reach & Impact Model. Incremental revenue = subscriptions shifted into the bundle × (revenue per bundle subscription − revenue per Plus subscription) Input Value Eligible reach, tour ~1,373 users/day Baseline ARPU / exposed, 21d $6.89 Cheap-path volume 82 paid subscriptions/day — none of them on the tour paywall Revenue per subscription, Plus $22.09 Revenue per subscription, bundle $50.59 Delta per shifted subscription $28.50 Upper bound on the cheap-path leak (all surfaces). 82 subs/day × $28.50 = ~$2,344/day , about $855K/year , if every cheap-path subscription moved to the bundle and nothing else changed. Addressable by a default tab on the tour paywall: ~$0/day — the tour already sells this segment nothing but the bundle. The gap is not a size problem, it is a surface problem. The segment is worth ~$9,459/day, so a +15% result needs ~$1,419/day of extra revenue. The leak is bigger than that — but all of it sits away from the tour: Where it is not. The tour paywall offers this segment only the bundle, so there is no cheaper purchase there to move. Where it is. Roughly 1,083 of the 1,235 cheap-path subscriptions come from feature paywalls and ad interstitials (Official Tabs, Smartscroll, transpose, autoscroll, AD 14Free Interstitial …), and 152 from the post-decline instant offer. The bundle still has no price on the feature surface. What that means for the test. A tour-only test cannot deliver +15% by moving users to a better product; it can only defend the current all-bundle mix — and adding a Pro tab puts a cheaper option in front of a segment that cannot choose one today, so the first-order risk on the tour is downside. Feature surface: not forecast. No bundle price exists off-tour, and the eligible population is unreliable until UMN-12572 lands. Recommendation. Re-scope version 1 onto the surfaces that carry the leak (feature paywalls, and the post-decline offer if it is brought back into scope), or state the tour test explicitly as a defensive read with a downside guardrail. A tour-only +15% target is not supported by the current product mix. Hypothesis If we open the Premium tab by default for iOS users in the top propensity decile ( segment = top , score >= -1 ) on the tour and feature paywalls, then ARPU per exposed user over 21 days will rise from $6.89 to $7.92 (+15%) over ~27 calendar days at 100% segment traffic (6.3 days of enrollment plus the 21-day metric window), without worsening refund 14d, cancel 14d, retention 7/14d, tour skip or store rating beyond thresholds still to be defined , because this segment already converts at a higher payment bar without paying less per head, so the binding constraint is which product it is shown first rather than its willingness to pay. Stated but reclassified: the original brief adds "without a drop in overall subscription conversion". Exp 7568 accepted exactly that drop as the cost of a higher-value mix. It is recorded here as a guardrail requiring a threshold, not as a condition of the hypothesis.
